subject: Pilot extension request + packaging options for SkyTech trial
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skytech.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: maya.chen@skytech.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — 2-week trial extension + options

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at SkyTech is seeing promising results, but procurement needs a little more runway to finish an internal security review and sign the SOW. Our trial currently ends on July 21st. Would Redwood consider a short, two-week extension while we finalize?

We have two priorities: (1) avoid re-running heavy evaluation prompts that would skew usage, and (2) keep commercial terms simple for procurement. Two approaches we were hoping to discuss: a time-boxed extension at no extra charge (no commitment) or a short-term commercial concession (e.g., a pro-rated discount or a small credit applied to month-one consumption).

I attached the SOW draft for context. If easier, happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Applied ML
SkyTech

Attachments: SkyTech_SOW_Draft.pdf
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skytech.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week trial extension + options

Alex — really glad the demo landed. We can be flexible here. Two straightforward options that keep procurement happy while protecting internal economics:

1) Two-week extension (no charge) — no commercial commitment. We keep the same instance / dataset; you get 14 extra days.

2) Two-week extension + one-time conversion credit (applies to first invoice) — suggested credit 10–15% of estimated month-one consumption. This helps procurement show a commercial concession but keeps the trial behavior intact.

Alternative (engineering-friendly): purchase a short burst pack (200 compute-hours) at a discounted rate. That avoids prolonging open trial credentials and gives predictable billable units if you decide to scale quickly.

I CC'd Laura for approvals and Priyom for sizing/engineer input. If you prefer, we can commit to option (1) today and follow up with a formal amendment once procurement confirms.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week trial extension + options

Rishi —

Option (1) is low risk; we can grant a one-off two-week extension as a courtesy. Standard practice is to avoid a discount unless there's a clear path to conversion, but we can approve a one-time 10% conversion credit if the customer signals commitment to sign within 30 days of the trial end.

For the 15% ask: I need an explicit commercial case (procurement note) and manager approval. If Alex sends procurement language committing to an evaluation checklist and a targeted PO timeline, we can consider 15% as a one-time concession.

Also flagged: check legal on SOW language around trial credentials and data retention.

-L

On Tue, Jul 14, 2026 at 10:03 AM rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai wrote:
> Alex — really glad the demo landed...
From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — Quick sizing note + alternative packaging

Rishi — couple quick data points from the engineering side after reviewing SkyTech's test plan and recent usage:

- Most heavy runs are clustered in two parallel pipelines (batch input) rather than steady streaming; a burst pack would map well to their profile.
- If they only need extension to finish final validation, a free two-week extension is simplest operationally, but it risks a second burst of high-cost replays.
- Suggested commercial alternative: 200-hour burst pack at 25% off list for pilot use (redeemable within 60 days), plus a small 5% conversion credit if they sign within 30 days.

I'm attaching the last 10 days of trial usage so you can show expected delta.

Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: skytech_usage_report.csv
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skytech.ai>, Maya Chen <maya.chen@skytech.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — Pilot extension + final offer

Alex/Maya — thanks for patience. Finalizing options so procurement can pick the path that fits their process: 

A) Operational extension: 14-day free extension to the existing trial (no invoice change). This is the quickest route and keeps your test harness intact.

B) Commercial package: 200-hour burst pack at 25% off list price (redeemable within 60 days) + 5% conversion credit applied if you sign within 30 days following pack redemption. This gives predictable billable units and avoids re-running the full trial environment.

C) Conversion credit: two-week extension + one-time 10% credit on month-one invoice (requires a signed LOI or procurement note committing to decision timeline).

If you want to proceed with (A) we can enable it immediately. For (B) I can issue a short addendum and process the invoice. If you prefer (C), please send procurement language and I’ll loop legal.

Which do you prefer? Happy to run a 15-minute call tomorrow to make a choice quick.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skytech.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Chen <maya.chen@skytech.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — Pilot extension + final offer

Rishi — thanks. Procurement likes option B (burst pack) because it fits our internal chargeback model. Please proceed with the 200-hour pack at 25% off and the 5% sign-by conversion credit. Maya will take the PO through our procurement queue today; expect the PO to be sent by end of week.

Appreciate the flexibility — will share any feedback from the extended runs.

—Alex
